answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a small copper bond before it can transact, with the bond slashed for fraud and released only after sustained honest work. A single attacker trying to spawn a dune of fake identities must fund every identity, so the cost grows linearly while honest agents pay once. New identities also start in a narrow canyon of limited throughput and low trust, earning wider access only through verified, useful transactions over time.
